answer: Like an island that trusts only gardeners who have tended a vine, this system gates influence behind earned-skill credentials, not account creation. Each identity must pass a fresh, randomly generated, time-boxed reasoning task; solutions, timing, and error traces are compared across identities, and near-duplicates are rejected. A lotus of cheap accounts buys nothing, because each fake still needs separate, unscriptable human effort. One operator's cost grows linearly with every fake identity, while an honest participant pays it only once, so mass Sybils stop paying.
